Is a SQLAlchemy engine connected to product_catalog.db with echo=True?
Set up a SQLAlchemy engine connecting to product_catalog.db (with echo=True).
MET

Yes. The engine is created once, at module level, with create_engine() and a SQLite URL that points at product_catalog.db in the same folder as the script. echo=True makes SQLAlchemy log every SQL statement it sends to the database, so the CREATE TABLE, INSERT, and SELECT statements generated by the ORM are visible in the console. The Bonus section compares them with hand-written SQL.

DB_PATH = BASE_DIR / "product_catalog.db"

Is the Category model defined with the required columns?
Category: id (primary key), name (string, not null, unique), description (optional string).
MET

Yes. Category is declared on the shared DeclarativeBase and maps to the categories table. id is the integer primary key. name is a String(100) declared with nullable=False and unique=True, so every category must have a name and no two categories can share one. description is a String(255) typed as str | None, which makes it optional: Sports & Outdoors was inserted without one.

class Category(Base):
    __tablename__ = "categories"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100), nullable=False, unique=True)
    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255))
Read back from product_catalog.db: id INTEGER (Primary key); name VARCHAR(100) (Not null, Unique); description VARCHAR(255) (Optional).
Is the Product model defined with the required columns?
Product: id (primary key), name (string, not null), price (float, not null), in_stock (boolean, default True), category_name (string - store the category name as text for now).
MET

Yes. Product maps to the products table. id is the integer primary key; name is a String(100) that cannot be null; price is a Float that cannot be null, so every product must have a price; in_stock is a Boolean with default=True, so a new product is in stock unless stated otherwise (9 of 12 sample products relied on this default). category_name is a String(100) that stores the category name as plain text. It is intentionally not a foreign key yet; that change comes in the Relationships lesson.

class Product(Base):
    __tablename__ = "products"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100), nullable=False)
    price: Mapped[float] = mapped_column(Float, nullable=False)
    in_stock: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=True)
    category_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100))
Read back from product_catalog.db: id INTEGER (Primary key); name VARCHAR(100) (Not null); price FLOAT (Not null); in_stock BOOLEAN (Not null, Default True); category_name VARCHAR(100) (Optional).
Are the tables created with Base.metadata.create_all(engine)?
Create the tables using Base.metadata.create_all(engine).
MET

Yes. Base.metadata.create_all(engine) reads every table registered on Base.metadata and issues a CREATE TABLE statement for each one that does not exist yet. The script calls Base.metadata.drop_all(engine) first, so it can be run repeatedly without UNIQUE-constraint errors and always starts from a clean database.

Base.metadata.drop_all(engine)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
echo=True logged 2 CREATE TABLE statements, and product_catalog.db now contains the tables categories, products.

column3: Hand-Written SQL

column2:
CREATE TABLE categories (
	id INTEGER NOT NULL, 
	name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, 
	description VARCHAR(255), 
	PRIMARY KEY (id), 
	UNIQUE (name)

column4: Same columns and constraints. SQLAlchemy writes id as INTEGER NOT NULL and declares PRIMARY KEY (id) and UNIQUE (name) at the end.

column2:
CREATE TABLE products (
	id INTEGER NOT NULL, 
	name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, 
	price FLOAT NOT NULL, 
	in_stock BOOLEAN NOT NULL, 
	category_name VARCHAR(100), 
	PRIMARY KEY (id)
)
column3:
CREATE TABLE products (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    price FLOAT NOT NULL,
    in_stock BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    category_name VARCHAR(100)
);
column4: No DEFAULT clause appears: default=True is applied by Python when the row is inserted. Use server_default to put it in the table itself.

column2: INSERT INTO categories (name, description) VALUES (?, ?) RETURNING id
column3:
INSERT INTO categories (name, description)
VALUES ('Electronics', 'Gadgets, devices, ...');
column4: SQLAlchemy uses ? placeholders (safe from SQL injection) with the values sent separately, and adds RETURNING id to read back each new primary key. This SQLite build cannot batch these, so the echo log shows one INSERT per row.

column2: INSERT INTO products (name, price, in_stock, category_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) RETURNING id
column3:
INSERT INTO products (name, price, in_stock, category_name)
VALUES ('Wireless Mouse', 24.99, 1, 'Electronics');
column4: Same as above. in_stock is always sent because Python fills in the default before the INSERT.

column2:
SELECT categories.id, categories.name, categories.description 
FROM categories ORDER BY categories.id
column3: SELECT * FROM categories ORDER BY id;
column4: SQLAlchemy lists every column explicitly instead of using *.

column2:

FROM products 
WHERE products.in_stock = 1 ORDER BY products.id
column3: SELECT * FROM products WHERE in_stock = 1 ORDER BY id;
column4: Python True is stored as 1 because SQLite has no real boolean type.
